sampling_model.design: Uniformly draw an ordered tuple of \(G_n\) pairwise-disjoint \(M\)-subsets of \(\mathcal U_n\), then independently and completely randomize exactly \(G_{1n}\) group labels to treatment.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) labeled units and every composition-indexed potential outcome are fixed; assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is shared within each realized group, with \(p_n=G_{1n}/G_n\to p\in(0,1)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The grouped-unit fraction satisfies \(N_n/n\to\rho\in[0,1]\); no birthday-scale condition on \(N_n^2/n\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no superpopulation nuisances. The latent object affecting exact variance is \(E_{\tau,1,n}\), the degree-one Johnson energy of the arm difference.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give asymptotic normality and CR2 ratio consistency for a fixed finite menu of admissible group sizes under shared boundedness, their Assumption 1, and \(N_n^2/n\to0\).
Theorem 3 and the Johnson-scheme discussion provide an orthogonal harmonic basis and common eigenspaces for functions on a slice.
Proposition 3.1 records the classical eigenvalues for distance graphs in the Johnson scheme, including the Kneser relation.
Theorems 3--4 establish finite-population Gaussian limits for complete randomization on fixed experimental units.
Theorem 1 makes CR2 exactly unbiased under a specified independent-cluster working covariance model.
Theorem 1 relates regression sandwich estimators to conservative Neyman variances when clusters are fixed.
The paper characterizes optimized estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference and complex designs because exact variance is generally unavailable.
Theorems 1--2 show that design-unbiased estimators can fail to concentrate under arbitrary or network interference.

body.tldr: Randomly formed groups cease to behave as independent regression clusters when a positive fraction of eligible units is partitioned. The exact normalized Kneser operator gives an unconditional finite-sample variance identity and a schedule-uniform expansion in which only the degree-one Johnson projection of the arm difference survives at first order; neither this expansion nor the CR2 variance comparison uses predictable-QV stabilization or scaled-variance nondegeneracy. Pointwise centered Gaussian inference and CR2 coverage are separate conditional conclusions for the named class that imposes predictable quadratic-variation stabilization for the unit-permutation-then-label-permutation filtration, together with nondegeneracy; bounded schedules alone are not claimed to imply that premise. CR2 estimates the independent-group term, so at positive density it is asymptotically conservative and is ratio-consistent exactly when the projection correction is negligible, conditional on the inference premises. When the sampling fraction vanishes, studentized normality holds without \(N_n^2/n\to0\), but this trades the comparator's Assumption 1 and birthday condition for the explicit filtration-side premise. The eight-unit witness has exact variance \(1/7\) and expected CR2 \(2/7\). Finally, the all-statistic variance-impossibility theorem holds already on the additive no-interference subclass and therefore transfers to arbitrary composition interference; its special Rademacher construction verifies predictable-QV stability separately and does not establish that property for every bounded schedule.

project_justification.gap: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} defines PAME and validates clustered inference by coupling the whole disjoint group tuple to independent draws under its Assumption 1 and \(N_n^2/n\to0\). That approximation discards first-order finite-pool dependence when \(N_n/n\to\rho>0\), while the fixed-cluster CR2 literature has no mechanism for restoring it. Bounded composition schedules by themselves also do not supply predictable quadratic-variation stabilization for the exact reveal filtration.
project_justification.niche: The disjointness relation is a Kneser operator on the uniform \(M\)-slice, so exact causal variance and the CR2 comparison can be decomposed unconditionally by Johnson degree before any Gaussian approximation is invoked. Inference is then layered on transparently for the named predictable-QV-stable class rather than presented as a consequence of boundedness.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact spectrum-weighted variance, the schedule-uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) dense expansion, and the unconditional CR2 fluctuation bound; proves that only degree one survives at the \(G_n\)-scale; and, under an explicitly separate filtration-side predictable-QV premise and scaled-variance nondegeneracy, derives a centered martingale CLT and Wald coverage. It also characterizes the CR2 sharpness frontier, verifies the versioned \({\tt clubSandwich}\) consumer and the finite witness, and proves an all-statistic exact-variance impossibility theorem using a construction-specific predictable-QV calculation and deterministic diagonal selection.

body.related_work: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} is the closest theorem-level comparator: its Section 3 permits a fixed finite menu of group sizes, and its Theorems 1--2 obtain asymptotic normality and CR2 ratio consistency under shared boundedness, their Assumption 1, and \(N_n^2/n\to0\). The present positive theory treats the exact homogeneous \(K=1\) structural subcase. Its exact Kneser variance and CR2 expansions are unconditional under the stated fixed-size design conditions, whereas its Gaussian and coverage conclusions replace the comparator's inference conditions by scaled-variance nondegeneracy and the explicit statistic-specific predictable-QV premise. This is an assumption trade, not a pure weakening, because predictable-QV stabilization is not derived for the full bounded-schedule class. Positive homogeneous conclusions are not claimed for variable group sizes. Theorems 1 and 3 and the Johnson association-scheme discussion of \cite{Filmus2016} provide the harmonic architecture; Proposition 3.1 of \cite{BrouwerEtAl2018} supplies the classical Kneser spectrum, and the present work derives the causal covariance quadratic form. Section 2.2 and Theorems 3--4 of \cite{LiDing2017} inform complete randomization, while \cite{Pollard1984}, Theorem VIII.1, supplies the martingale-array implication after predictable variation and conditional Lindeberg have been established or imposed as stated. The versioned \({\tt clubSandwich}\) 0.7.0 and \({\tt sandwich}\) 3.1-3 source contracts supply the software assembly, default-target, adjustment, bread, and scale semantics used by the exact consumer proposition; \cite{PustejovskyTipton2018} explains CR2 calibration under independent-cluster working models, and \cite{SuDing2021} gives the fixed-cluster design-based regression comparison. None supplies the random-partition projection correction. \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} studies optimized estimable conservative quadratic bounds when exact variance is inaccessible, and \cite{BasseAiroldi2018} supplies general interference nonconcentration logic; neither subsumes the proved equal-observation dense-PAME lower bound. That lower bound holds on an additive no-interference subclass and hence transfers to the full arbitrary-composition class. \cite{AronowGreenLee2014} gives sharp variance bounds for ordinary complete randomization, whereas global composition-table completion is a distinct unselected seed. \cite{BasseDingFellerToulis2024} and \cite{PuelzBasseFellerToulis2022} obtain exact tests by making peer-effect nulls sharp through symmetry or conditioning; PAME remains non-sharp from one random partition.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Finite-sample CR2 conservativeness is not asserted: the exact bias is \(-C_{\tau\tau,n}\), and higher Johnson eigenvalues alternate in sign. Conservativeness emerges at the \(G_n\)-scale because only the negative degree-one eigenvalue survives. Predictable quadratic-variation stabilization is a filtration-side conditional premise for the general CLT and coverage results, not a consequence proved from bounded schedules; its verification for the Rademacher lower-bound priors is construction-specific. The Rademacher variance limits are separated only when \(\rho>0\); at \(\rho=0\) their gap vanishes. The \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2})\) CR2 fluctuation bound is only an upper bound, so \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\) is a benchmark crossover rather than a proved exact noise-order elbow. Positive results are restricted to the homogeneous fixed-size design.
body.honest_scope: The exact Kneser covariance, finite-sample design variance, schedule-uniform dense projection expansion, and CR2 variance expansion are unconditional design-based conclusions under group-count growth, stable treatment and sampling fractions, fixed \(M\), and bounded potential outcomes; scaled-variance nondegeneracy and predictable-QV stabilization are not used for those conclusions. The centered martingale CLT, CR2 studentized limits, Wald coverage, and sparse studentization conclusion are conditional on the separately named predictable-QV-stable class, with scaled-variance nondegeneracy where division by the asymptotic variance is required. No claim is made that bounded schedules establish predictable-QV stabilization. The sparse result drops \(N_n^2/n\to0\) but trades the comparator's Assumption 1 for that filtration-side premise. The exact software identity is tied to the stated equal-group unweighted intercept-plus-binary-treatment call and versioned package semantics. The impossibility theorem assumes \(G_n\to\infty\), \(p_n\to p\in(0,1)\), and \(N_n/n\to\rho\in(0,1]\), holds on additive no-interference schedules, and therefore transfers upward to arbitrary composition interference; its Rademacher priors satisfy predictable-QV stability by a separate construction-specific theorem. When \(\rho=0\), the projection correction and Rademacher limit gap vanish. No finite-sample CR2 conservativeness or variable-group-size extension is asserted.
